subject: chemistry
title: Solubility rules and making insoluble salts
key_idea: The solubility rules tell you whether a salt dissolves in water. When two solutions are mixed and an insoluble salt could form, it appears as a precipitate. You separate it by filtering, washing with distilled water and drying.

blocks.text: These general rules describe which common compounds dissolve in water. You need to recall them.

rows: Silver chloride and lead chloride are insoluble
Lead, barium and calcium sulfates are insoluble
Sodium, potassium and ammonium ones are soluble

items: All sodium, potassium and ammonium salts and all nitrates are soluble.
Chlorides and sulfates are soluble, with the exceptions in the table.
Carbonates and hydroxides are insoluble, except sodium, potassium and ammonium.

blocks.text: When two solutions are mixed, the two compounds swap partners. If one of the new compounds is insoluble, it forms a precipitate.

items.meaning: An insoluble solid formed when two solutions are mixed.

items.text: Barium chloride + sodium sulfate gives barium sulfate and sodium chloride.

items.lead: Check each new compound against the rules.
items.text: Sodium chloride is soluble. Barium sulfate is an exception, so it is insoluble.
Barium sulfate is the precipitate. If both new compounds are soluble, there is no precipitate.

blocks.text: You will see a solid form, or the mixture go cloudy. You will not see fizzing or bubbles.

diagram.alt: Pick two solutions to mix and see whether a precipitate forms and what it is called.

options.label: Barium chloride + sodium sulfate
options.explanation: Barium sulfate is an insoluble sulfate. Sodium chloride is soluble.

options.label: Copper sulfate + sodium hydroxide
options.explanation: Hydroxides are insoluble, except sodium, potassium and ammonium.

options.label: Potassium carbonate + calcium nitrate
options.explanation: Carbonates are insoluble, except sodium, potassium and ammonium. Potassium nitrate is soluble.

options.label: Iron(II) sulfate + sodium hydroxide
options.explanation: Iron(II) hydroxide is an insoluble hydroxide.

options.label: Silver nitrate + sodium chloride
options.explanation: Silver chloride is an exception to the rule that chlorides are soluble.

options.label: Lead nitrate + sodium sulfate
options.explanation: Lead sulfate is an exception to the rule that sulfates are soluble.

options.label: Magnesium chloride + sodium hydroxide
options.explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is an insoluble hydroxide.

options.label: Sodium chloride + potassium nitrate
options.explanation: All sodium and potassium salts are soluble, so nothing is insoluble.

items: Swap partners, then check both new compounds against the solubility rules.
An insoluble compound forms a precipitate. Name it.
A precipitate looks like a solid forming, or the mixture going cloudy.

sections.heading: Making a pure, dry insoluble salt

blocks.text: An insoluble salt is made by mixing two solutions. It must then be separated from the solution, washed and dried.

diagram.alt: Put the steps for obtaining a pure, dry insoluble salt in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps for a pure, dry sample of a precipitate in order
steps: Mix the two solutions so the precipitate forms
Filter the mixture through filter paper in a funnel
Wash the solid on the filter paper with distilled water
Leave the solid to dry in a warm place

items: Filtering separates the solid precipitate from the solution.
Washing with distilled water removes traces of the other solution, so the salt is pure.
Drying can be done in a warm place, an oven or with filter paper. Do not use crystallisation.
The other salt stays dissolved in the filtrate. Pour the filtrate into an evaporating basin and heat to evaporate the water to get it as a solid.
Filter, wash with distilled water, then dry.
Do not heat or evaporate the mixture before filtering.

checks.q: Name the white precipitate formed when barium chloride solution reacts with dilute sulfuric acid.
Silver nitrate solution is mixed with sodium chloride solution. Name the precipitate that forms and explain how you know.
checks.a: Silver chloride. Chlorides are soluble except those of silver and lead, so silver chloride is insoluble. Sodium nitrate is soluble.

checks.q: Describe how to obtain a pure, dry sample of a precipitate from the reaction mixture.
checks.a: Filter the mixture, wash the solid with distilled water, then dry it (for example in a warm place).

exam_phrases: wash / rinse the solid with distilled water
leave in a warm place / put in an oven
pour the filtrate into an evaporating basin and heat to evaporate the water

mistakes.wrong: Heat the mixture to evaporate the water and crystallise the precipitate.
mistakes.right: Crystallisation is rejected for a precipitate. If you heat to evaporate all the water before filtering, you score nothing. Filter, wash, then dry.
'Dry it out' or 'dry it off' alone is not allowed. Say how: in an oven, on a windowsill, with filter paper, or leave in a warm place.

mistakes.wrong: Wash the solid after it has been dried.
mistakes.right: The washing mark is not given if washing is done after drying. Filter, wash, then dry.

mistakes.wrong: A precipitate forms, and bubbles are seen.
mistakes.right: 'Precipitate' alone is ignored and any answer with fizzing or bubbles is rejected. Say a solid forms, or the mixture goes cloudy.

worked_example.question:
When barium hydroxide solution is neutralised by dilute sulfuric acid, a white precipitate of barium sulfate is formed in the conical flask.
Describe an experiment to obtain a sample of pure, dry barium sulfate from the contents of the conical flask.
answer_points: Filter the contents of the flask to collect the barium sulfate.
Wash the barium sulfate on the filter paper (with distilled water).
Leave it to dry in a warm place.
worked_example.tip: The washing and drying marks depend on filtering. Crystallisation is rejected, and washing must come before drying.
